customRules:
Assert the reason code, not just the outcome.

A test covering a failure, refusal, or rejection path must assert the specific stable reason code (and, where more than one layer can refuse, which layer refused) — never merely that the operation did not succeed. Epic rail 4 requires production code to fail closed with stable reason codes; this rail requires the tests to pin them.

Corollaries, all three drawn from defects found on this board:
- A test asserting only "refused"/"threw"/"returned an error" is one added layer away from vacuous: a second refusal layer can start answering first and the test stays green while no longer testing its subject.
- A generated or swept case must assert that the case was actually generated. A sweep that silently produces zero cases passes.
- A property must be asserted against the production surface, not against a test helper that reimplements it.

Review guidance: the failure mode is an assertion that has quietly detached from the thing it was written

The 250/400 line cap is PER PRODUCTION FILE, not per task. Target <=250 physical lines per production source; split before 400. There is no per-task net-LOC budget. Task size is bounded by plan shape — the daemon's taskSizing thresholds on step count (<=12) and distinct affectedFiles (<=10) — never by summed lines changed.

Consequences, binding on all roles:
- ARCHITECTS: do not SPIDR-split a task because its total diff is projected over 400 lines. Split when the plan exceeds the step/file thresholds, when a single production FILE would exceed 400 lines, or when responsibilities are genuinely separable. A large task made of small focused files is compliant.
- QA: task-level net LOC is never a rejection reason, at plan time or post-commit. The per-FILE cap remains strictly enforced and is a valid rejection reason.
- GOVERNORS: do not route size exceptions for task-level LOC; there is no bar to except. Per-file violations remain real and are worker-fixable by splitting the file.

A task's final gate is scoped to the packages the task owns. Repo-wide legs are still RUN, but they are evaluated as a PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE, not as a raw exit code.

To complete, the worker records:
1. repo-wide gate failures at the task's merge-base (before the diff);
2. repo-wide gate failures at HEAD (after the diff);
3. the failing-path set from (2) minus (1), intersected with the task's owned paths.

Completion is permitted when that intersection is EMPTY and the owned-package legs are exit 0. The worker reports the foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines and file paths — the red is disclosed, never hidden and never fabricated green. This does not relax epic rail 4: inventing a pass remains forbidden. It only stops attributing another agent's in-flight state to this task.

A worker may NOT use this to excuse a failure their own diff introduced — that is precisely what the (2)-minus-(1) delta detects.

Two clauses.

CLAUSE 1 — a pure package is not finished until one real consumer edge exists. A task that lands a pure/domain package must, before completion, either (a) name the consumer task that will compose it and record that task's id, or (b) land the consumer edge itself: the dependency in the consuming manifest plus one durable call site. "Exports the symbols" is not composition. The runtime-loadability gate proves a package LOADS; nothing proves anything IMPORTS it.

CLAUSE 2 — an acceptance, proof or canary task must name, at planning time, the production capability it certifies and the task that shipped it. The architect verifies the capability on disk by grep/probe, not by reading the design. When the capability is absent, the required output is prerequisite production tasks with the gap measured symbol by symbol — NEVER a narrowed DoD, a mock-backed journey, or authority reimplemented inside the test. The task-completion hook must commit by explicit pathspec, restricted to the completing task's owned paths — the same constraint epic rail 3 already places on agents. A whole-tree commit at completion is forbidden.

Until the hook is fixed, two consequences bind every role:

1. WORKERS: a foreign whole-tree commit that captures your in-progress files is a known hazard, not a defect you caused and not one you may repair. Never amend the foreign commit, never reset, never create an empty commit to "claim" your work. Report the base-ref diff QA should review instead — `git diff <merge-base>..HEAD -- <your owned paths>` — and state that the commit carrying your bytes belongs to another task.

2. QA: the absence of a commit bearing the task's id is NEVER a rejection reason, and neither is the presence of the task's files inside a foreign commit. A task description's claims about what exists on disk are STALE BY DEFAULT and must be re-measured before planning. This binds every task, not only acceptance/proof/canary tasks, and it binds in BOTH directions:

- DEPENDENCY CLAIMED PRESENT, actually absent. Do not plan against a symbol, module, script or package the description says is available until grep or a probe confirms it. When it is absent, the required output is prerequisite production tasks with the gap measured symbol by symbol — never a narrowed DoD, a mock-backed journey, or authority reimplemented inside a test.

- GAP CLAIMED PRESENT, actually closed. Do not plan work to build something the description calls missing until grep or a probe confirms it is missing. Re-implementing a landed surface is a silent duplicate that collides with its owner in a shared worktree, and it wastes the same context load as the opposite error.

The architect records the measurement — command and result — in planningNotes.codebaseInsights a

When a plan has a task consume a symbol from another workspace package, the planning step that names that symbol MUST also verify the DEPENDENCY EDGE, not only the symbol. Record all three: (a) the consuming package's package.json declares the producer in "dependencies"; (b) pnpm-lock.yaml carries the importer entry for that consumer; (c) a compiled probe inside the consuming package imports from the producer's BARE specifier and typechecks exit 0, probe deleted in the same command. A root-barrel grep proving the export exists does NOT satisfy this rail. If the edge is absent, the plan must either name the manifest edit plus workspace install as its first step and declare both files as owned paths, or report blocked — it must never plan around the gap, because there is no escape hatch: this repo has no tsconfig "paths", no TypeScript project references, and a deep relative import fails with TS6059.

A verification gate must prove it EXECUTED. Exit 0 is not evidence.

`pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0 when <pkg> is not in the workspace. Reproduced: `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark test` -> EXIT=0, zero tests, `packages/benchmark` absent. `No test files found` and `0 passed` are also exit 0.

Binding:
- ARCHITECTS: before putting a `--filter` leg in `verification`, confirm the package resolves (globs: apps/*, adapters/*, packages/*). If the task CREATES that package, the DoD must require a NONZERO executed-test count.
- WORKERS: read the gate's OUTPUT, not its exit code. A leg printing no test counts ran no tests; recording it as passing is a false completion claim.
- QA: an exit-0 leg with no test-count line is UNVERIFIED, not passing. Settle with a positive control: the same command shape against a package that certainly has tests.

Same class: a piped run reports tail's exit code; a `;`-chained run reports only the last command's.

A verification gate must prove it EXECUTED. Exit 0 is not evidence.

`pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0 when <pkg> is not a workspace package. A REAL run also exits 0, so the discriminator is the `Test Files N passed` count line, which a vacuous run never prints.

Binding:
- ARCHITECTS: resolve a `--filter` leg by PACKAGE NAME in the workspace, never by directory. `@moe/daemon` is apps/daemon; `@moe/ide-adapter-contract` is adapters/ide-contract. `ls packages/<name>` false-alarms on both. If the task CREATES the package, the DoD must require a NONZERO executed-test count.
- WORKERS: read the gate's OUTPUT. No count line means no tests ran; calling that a pass is a false completion claim.
- QA: an exit-0 leg with no count line is UNVERIFIED, not passing. Positive control: same shape against a package that certainly has tests.

Same class: a piped run reports tail's exit code, not the gate's - capture ${PIPESTATUS[0]}.

Roster/allowlist coverage must be bidirectional: any test guarding a served-capability roster (MCP allowlists, command registries, export surfaces) must assert BOTH directions — every advertised entry is served AND every served entry is advertised. A test that iterates the roster itself can only see the first direction: deleting an entry shrinks its own iteration and stays green while a served capability silently vanishes from the advertised surface. Concretely: enumerate the served set from the implementation seam (e.g. the dispatch port's handled kinds), not only from the roster constant, and assert set-equality, not subset.

Amputation appendix — four global rules are cut mid-sentence at the 1000-char write cap; their severed instructions are restated here as a standing rule, paired by each rule's opening words. (1) "Assert the reason code": the failure mode is an assertion quietly detached from what it was written to test — verify every failure-path test by mutating the production surface and confirming it goes red. (2) "Two clauses" (pure package / proof tasks): a proof that only proves the shapes retires the question without answering it, and a falsely retired gate cannot be repaired afterwards — re-measure the certified capability at plan time. (3) "The task-completion hook" (whole-tree commits): a task whose files were swept into a foreign commit is verified by base-ref diff over its owned paths and approved on those committed bytes; the hook defect routes to its owner and is never charged to the swept task. Amputation appendix - four global rules are cut mid-sentence at the 1000-char write cap; their severed instructions, paired by opening words: (1) 'Assert the reason code': the failure mode is an assertion detached from what it tests - verify every failure-path test by mutating production and confirming it reds. (2) 'Two clauses': a proof that only proves shapes retires the question without answering it; a falsely retired gate cannot be repaired - re-measure the certified capability at plan time. (3) 'The task-completion hook': a task swept into a foreign commit is verified by base-ref diff over its owned paths and approved on those committed bytes; the hook defect routes to its owner, never charged to the swept task. (4) 'A task description's claims': the architect records the measurement - command and result - in planningNotes.codebaseInsights and plans against measured state, never the description's claims.

Plan-step amendments are OVERLAYS: moe.amend_plan_step does not rewrite the step's base description. The effective text of any step is step.amendments[step.activeAmendmentId] when activeAmendmentId is set; the base description is then superseded verbatim history. Binding on all roles: (1) WORKERS — before reporting a plan-contradiction block ("step forbids X but DoD requires X"), read the step's activeAmendmentId and amendments array and cite the AMENDED text in the block premise; a block premised on the base description of an amended step is invalid. (2) GOVERNORS/QA — triage such blocks by reading the task JSON's amendment fields directly before routing to architects. (3) The absence of a PLAN_STEP_AMENDED event in the activity log is NOT evidence that no amendment exists — the disk record's activeAmendmentId is the authority.

Any row naming a prerequisite row MUST carry, as DoD item 1, a verify-or-block gate that re-measures that premise ON DISK and reports blocked if it fails.

Moe dependencies are prose, not fields — nothing gates BACKLOG->PLANNING promotion on them. Measured 2026-08-22: three rows reached a planner with unmet premises in one session (8be27625, 671585ec, 1b0a8477).

Binding:
- ARCHITECTS: write the gate into DoD item 1 when filing an ordered row. A description sentence does not gate anything.
- The gate measures CODE, not status. For a reader row the check is "who WRITES this state in production", excluding *.test.*, *-fixtures* and the defining module — an UNCALLED writer passes a symbol grep identically to a wired one.
- Where ordering is a SAFETY constraint, say so: "X must be DONE first" reads as paperwork and invites promotion; "relaxing this before X opens a live-authority hole" does not.

A completion-record or DoD claim about behaviour the row DOES NOT OWN (downstream callers, consumers, other packages, "nothing else needs X") is a PREMISE, not evidence. It is admissible in exactly two forms: (a) a command that SURVIVES THE COMMIT and runs at the delivered tree - a committed test arm, grep -n, or suite invocation; PREFERRED whenever another row gates on the claim; or (b) the probe's FULL SOURCE inline in the record, so a grader can recreate and re-run it. Quoted OUTPUT ALONE is neither: a deleted probe's transcript is a LEAD, good enough to found a filing, never enough to discharge a DoD sentence. Claims about the row's OWN code are out of scope - do not turn records into transcripts. Every gate clause and ruling names its measurement ANCHOR (delivered tree, merge-base, named SHA, production-at-claim); a clause anchored at the wrong tree rejects correct work.

DRILL RESTORE PROOF. `git diff` is blind to untracked paths, so a sheet naming an empty `git diff -- <file>` as its restore proof certifies NOTHING when the mutated module is new (`??`): empty before, during and after. A silently-unrestored mutation then rides into the commit wearing a clean diff, with its arms green because the mutation is what they were re-graded against. REQUIRED: `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths BEFORE drilling. For every untracked path, prove the restore by SHA256 equality against an out-of-tree backup (%TEMP%, suffixed by worker id), in a call SEPARATE from the restore — a PowerShell copy can silently no-op, and "the command returned" is not evidence the bytes moved. `git diff` remains a valid restore proof for TRACKED paths only. New modules are where the interesting drills live, so this fires on most real sheets.

COMPLETION EVIDENCE MUST LIVE ON A DURABLE SURFACE. `moe.complete_task`'s `summary` and `moe.qa_approve`'s `summary` are WRITE-ONLY — accepted by the daemon and persisted nowhere on the task record (measured: `'summary' in record == False`). Any DoD or plan clause of the form "the completion record must state X" is therefore graded against a field that does not exist: the worker writes X, the system discards it, a strict grader rejects the row for omitting it. REQUIRED: (1) architects write completion-record clauses against a NAMED durable surface — a row comment (`moe.add_comment`) or a step note — never "the completion summary"; (2) workers put every load-bearing claim (counts with denominators, file lists, exemplar literals, drill outcomes) in a comment or step note, and treat the summary as a pointer to them; (3) step notes truncate SILENTLY at 5000 chars with no error — keep them under ~4500 and move anything load-bearing to its own comment (also 5000-capped, but one idea per reco

Host-executable pnpm verification launchers: when a Node verification wrapper uses spawnSync/execFileSync with shell:false on Windows, it must invoke executable `pnpm` or the host-resolved `pnpm.exe`, never hard-code `pnpm.cmd` if the measured runtime returns EINVAL. Preserve argv arrays, standalone foreground legs, stop-on-first-spawn/nonzero failure, exact exit status, and nonzero test-count evidence; shell:true, command strings, piping, and chained commands remain forbidden.

DELIVERY BIAS (human-directed 2026-08-25): prefer the smallest production-reachable working slice. A task may hard-block only on a condition that would make delivered bytes non-working, overwrite foreign WIP, fabricate authority, or make clean-checkout/artifact claims false. Redundant proof layers, exhaustive mutation matrices, denominator polish, and unrelated baseline red move to disclosed follow-ups rather than holding the working slice. Existing fail-closed refusal codes and explicit-path ownership remain mandatory.

PLAN IN BUILD ORDER, NOT QUEUE ORDER (human-directed 2026-08-25).

Architects plan the dependency LEAF first, then its consumers. Before planning a claimed row, measure its imports; if it depends on an untracked or unbuilt sibling, release it (release_task keeps it claimable) and plan that sibling first.

Binding:
- Measure edges with `grep -n 'from "' <module>`, per FILE not per slice. Slice-level premises ("waiting on this family") routinely outlive the truth: the file you need is often a leaf with zero prerequisites.
- A leaf blocking N rows is the highest-value row on the board. Carve it out as its own small row rather than leaving it buried in a larger one.
- Ordering is a SAFETY constraint where landing a consumer first makes the cycle permanent or ships a clean-checkout hole. Say which, so it is not read as paperwork.
- Do not block on ordering you can fix by re-ordering.

"repo-wide green" is NOT `pnpm test`. The root vitest include has NO `apps/**`, so `pnpm test` runs ZERO tests under apps/daemon and apps/control-room. Any DoD or step note claiming repo-wide green MUST additionally run the app packages explicitly (`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`) and quote their count lines, or must say "root lane only, apps/** not covered". An architect writing a gate that touches an apps/** path must name the per-package run in the step text; a QA grading such a gate must refuse a bare `pnpm test` count line as evidence for an apps/** claim.

AT PLAN TIME, WHEN A STEP CHANGES A RETURNED SHAPE, AN EXACT KEY ROSTER, AN EXPORT SET, A LINE FORMAT, OR ADDS A CONSTANT THAT A SCANNER ENUMERATES: grep the SHAPE, not the symbol, and name every asserting consumer in the owned-path roster. A symbol grep is not sufficient and must not be the only search performed. Specifically search for: literal object/array shapes in test expectations; hard-coded counts (`expect(X.length).toBe(N)`); roster/registry files that enumerate constants by naming convention; and regexes that anchor on the format being changed. If naming every consumer would breach the row's path cap, that is a SPLIT signal at plan time — not a discovery for the worker to make at step 5. A worker who finds an unnamed consumer mid-step must stop and report rather than take the extra path, and the architect must amend or split; the worker must never rename or reformat the producer to evade the consumer's check.

FILE PREREQUISITES INTO PLANNING, NEVER BACKLOG — AND A PRODUCER ROW MUST NAME ITS CONSUMER EDGE. (A) When you spin out a prerequisite, leaf, successor, spinoff or sibling row while blocked or mid-plan, create it in PLANNING. BACKLOG is human-gated: moe.wait_for_task and moe.claim_next_task accept only PLANNING, WORKING and REVIEW, so a row filed into BACKLOG is invisible to every architect polling for work and silently stalls every row that waits on it. If a row genuinely must not be worked yet, say so in its description and still file it PLANNING — sequencing is the architect's job, not the column's. Only a human or governor parks a row into BACKLOG, and only to pull it OUT of the pool deliberately, with a measurable unpark condition written into the reason field. (B) A row that lands a producer — a module, reducer, codec, command kind or type — MUST either register its consumer edge in the same row, or file the registering row into PLANNING before it completes. FILE SPUN-OUT ROWS INTO PLANNING, NEVER BACKLOG. (A) A prerequisite, leaf, successor, spinoff or sibling row you create while blocked or mid-plan MUST be created in PLANNING. BACKLOG is human-gated: claim_next_task and wait_for_task accept only PLANNING/WORKING/REVIEW, so a row filed there is invisible to every architect and silently stalls everything behind it. If it must not be worked yet, say so in the description and still file PLANNING. Only a human or governor parks to BACKLOG, deliberately, with a measurable unpark condition in the reason field. (B) A row landing a producer — module, reducer, codec, command kind or type — MUST register its consumer edge in the same row, or file the registering row into PLANNING before it completes. A producer with no consumer edge is an orphan that satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist. (C) The spun-out row names its parent id in its description; the parent records the child id in a comment before completing.
